s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity weakness with sensory changes and autonomic dysfunction
salient_findings: Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
key_facts: 61-year-old woman with type II diabetes
1-year history of progressive lower-extremity weakness
100-lb unintentional weight loss
Weakness began in proximal left leg and gradually involved right leg and both hands
Worsening numbness and tingling in feet
Became wheelchair-dependent within 6 months
Denies pain, flank pain, hematuria, fevers, visual changes, speech or swallowing difficulty
Cranial nerves II–XII were intact
Sensation to light touch was reduced in feet
Impairment of vibration and proprioception
Reflexes were 2+ in upper extremities and absent at knees and ankles
Plantar responses were flexor
Bladder catheterization yielded 1.8 L of retained urine
Laboratory studies showed normal complete blood count and low sodium
CSF analysis revealed elevated protein and normal glucose
Electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrated chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy

differentials: Multifocal acquired demyelinating sensory and motor neuropathy
per_call: Multifocal acquired demyelinating sensory and motor neuropathy

shortlist.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes with elevated CSF protein and demyelinating polyneuropathy on electromyography

shortlist.label: Diabetic amyotrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Type II diabetes and progressive lower-extremity weakness with weight loss

shortlist.label: Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral femoral nerve enlargement on MRI and chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy

shortlist.label: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower-extremity weakness and sensory changes with atrophy of hands and thighs

shortlist.label: Cauda equina syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Urinary retention and bilateral lower-extremity weakness with reduced sensation and absent reflexes

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive lower-extremity weakness, worsening numbness and tingling in feet, and significant weight loss, along with electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrating chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy and superimposed chronic lumbosacral plexopathy, supports this diagnosis. The absence of pain and the pattern of weakness also align with lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy, particularly in the context of diabetes.

rejected.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
rejected.why: While the electromyography and nerve conduction studies show demyelinating polyneuropathy, the pattern of progression and the presence of significant weight loss and lumbosacral plexopathy features are more suggestive of lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy.

rejected.label: Diabetic amyotrophy
rejected.why: Diabetic amyotrophy typically presents with severe pain, which the patient denies, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
rejected.why: This is a hereditary condition that typically presents earlier in life and does not account for the significant weight loss or the specific pattern of nerve involvement seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Cauda equina syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has urinary retention, the absence of other typical features such as saddle anesthesia and the presence of a more gradual onset of symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.
